added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite names no base gate log (the base arm was not run within the fence), so the added-failure count was not taken; after_suite names gate-head.log, which reports 324 passed with no failing node id

findings.text: follow-on: except (OSError, ValueError) does not catch flight.FlightConfigError (a plain Exception subclass) that read_layer_file raises on a duplicate-key or malformed catalogue; reproduced by pointing RECKON_MODEL_CATALOGUE at a catalogue with a duplicate key, where ledger.build_record raises FlightConfigError instead of returning, so this node adds a new path by which a malformed catalogue stops every ledger write.

follow-on: the subscription_backends block, and capabilities.derive_routing's new billing key, are covered by no assertion in the node's tests or the suite, so a regression that drops or mis-keys them would not redden any test.

follow-on: the module docstring says lanes are declared in the model catalogue (subscription_groups), a key that does not exist, while the implementation rides budget_group with a -sub suffix and the manifest records that a top-level subscription_groups key was rejected by the flight schema.

follow-on: test_metered_backend_cost_is_unchanged still names claude as its metered example and asserts its cost is kept; it passes only because the autouse conftest shield points RECKON_MODEL_CATALOGUE at an absent file, so its green is an artefact rather than evidence that metered billing is unchanged.

follow-on: backend_budget_group re-implements the backend-to-budget_group lookup owned by reckon/crew/budget_group.py, which this node declared as a write path but did not extend, and reads the raw catalogue rather than resolved flight config, so a host or project override of budget_group is ignored by the ledger while flight honours it.
